title: Enrichment for kubernetes metadata doesn't populate into ES with EKS 1.24
body:
## Bug Report

I don't see k8s metadata in elasticsearch, tried different options including switching to kubelet. Probably there is some misconfiguration or lack of permissions. Can you please check what's wrong?

**To Reproduce**
Deploy fluentbit helm chart 0.28.0 with below config

**Expected behavior**
K8s meta data like pod name, namespace are populated into elasticsearch

- Steps to reproduce the problem:


**Your Environment**
<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->
* Version used: fluent bit 2.1.2, helm chart 0.28.0
* Configuration:

fluent-bit clusterrole:
```
rules:
- apiGroups:
  - ""
  resources:
  - namespaces
  - pods
  verbs:
  - get
  - list
  - watch
```
fluent-bit helm chart config:
```yaml
config:
  ## https://<redacted-host>/manual/pipeline/inputs
  inputs: |
    [INPUT]
        Name              tail
        Tag               kube.myapp.*
        multiline.parser  docker, cri
        Path              /var/log/containers/*airflow*.log
        DB                /var/log/flb_kube_airflow.db
        Mem_Buf_Limit     5MB
        Skip_Long_Lines   Off
        Refresh_Interval  10


  ## https://<redacted-host>/manual/pipeline/filters
  filters: |
    [FILTER]
        Name kubernetes
        Match kube.*
        Merge_Log On
        Merge_Parser catchall
        Keep_Log Off
        K8S-Logging.Parser On
        K8S-Logging.Exclude Off
        Buffer_Size         0
        Kube_Meta_Cache_TTL 300s

  ## https://<redacted-host>/manual/pipeline/outputs
  outputs: |
    [OUTPUT]
        Name es
        Match kube.myapp.*
        Host elasticsearch.logs
        Logstash_Format On
        Logstash_Prefix airflow
        Retry_Limit False
        Suppress_Type_Name On


  customParsers: |
    [PARSER]
        Name        custom_docker
        Format      regex
        Regex       ^(?<time>[^ ]+) (?<stream>[^ ]+) (?<flags>[^ ]+) (?<log>.+)$
        Time_Key    time
        Time_Format %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%L
        Time_Keep   On

    [PARSER]
        Name    catchall
        Format  regex
        Regex   ^(?<message>.*)$
```
* Environment name and version (e.g. Kubernetes? What version?): eks 1.24
* Server type and version: https://github.com/awslabs/amazon-eks-ami/releases/tag/v20230203
* Operating System and version: `Amazon Linux 2`
```
kernel: 5.4.228-131.415.amzn2
dockerd: 20.10.17-1.amzn2.0.1
containerd: 1.6.6-1.amzn2.0.2
runc: 1.1.4-1.amzn2
```
* Filters and plugins: default

comments.body:
If I'm correctthe error should be [here](https://github.com/fluent/fluent-bit/blob/master/plugins/filter_kubernetes/kube_meta.c#L1262), however, I'm not entirely sure. In your configuration you're not defining `kube_tag_prefix` which means it holds its default value of `kube.var.log.containers.` and the tag you've set in the input plugin is `kube.myapp.*` which by the way unless I'm wrong should be `kube.myapp` (because `kube.myapp.*` is the regular expression used by the filters and output plugins to match tags while routing).

So if you wanted to make some tests I'd suggest modifying the value of `tag` in your input plugin and maybe if you can adding this block before the kubernetes filter : 

```
    [FILTER]
        Name stdout
        Match kube.*
```

Which should dump the lines before they go through the filter and will help us compare the tag with the value of `kube_tag_prefix` to properly understand the error.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Ah, I know the issue here as I had the same.

The key is knowing what is happening here: https://<redacted-host>/manual/pipeline/filters/kubernetes#workflow-of-tail-+-kubernetes-filter

Using the config below, tail input on K8S will give you a tag like so: `kube.var.log.containers.<pod_namespace_etc>` 
The reason is that is how the file is actually named on disk - the dots replace the directory and the config specifies the prefix of `kube.`.

```text
[INPUT]
    Name    tail
    Tag     kube.*
    Path    /var/log/containers/*.log

[FILTER]
    Name             kubernetes
    Match            kube.*
    Kube_Tag_Prefix  kube.var.log.containers.
```

The K8S filter then strips off the `kube_tag_prefix` which defaults to `kube.var.log.containers` as indicated in the docs. This is to get the pod name, namespace and container to then query the K8S API.
However, in your original configuration you have changed the default prefix so you also need to specify the new prefix - this is why you are getting extra stuff in the query for the pod name.

@reporter this is what you need to do - I've only included the relevant options to simplify:
```text
    [INPUT]
        Name              tail
        Tag                  kube.myapp.*

    [FILTER]
        Name kubernetes
        Match kube.*
        Kube_Tag_Prefix  kube.myapp.var.log.containers.
```

comments.body:
I also have no issue with using the merge parser, it works fine if I specify it as you did.
```
config:
  ## https://<redacted-host>/manual/pipeline/inputs
  inputs: |
    [INPUT]
        Name              tail
        Tag               kube.myapp.*
        multiline.parser  docker, cri
        Path              /var/log/containers/*.log
        Mem_Buf_Limit     5MB
        Skip_Long_Lines   On
        Refresh_Interval  10
        Exclude_Path      *fluent-bit*.log


  ## https://<redacted-host>/manual/pipeline/filters
  filters: |
    [FILTER]
        Name kubernetes
        Match kube.*
        Merge_Log On
        Keep_Log Off
        K8S-Logging.Parser On
        K8S-Logging.Exclude On
        Kube_Tag_Prefix  kube.myapp.var.log.containers.
        Merge_Parser catchall

  ## https://<redacted-host>/manual/pipeline/outputs
  outputs: |
    [OUTPUT]
        Name stdout
        Match *

  customParsers: |
    [PARSER]
        Name        custom_docker
        Format      regex
        Regex       ^(?<time>[^ ]+) (?<stream>[^ ]+) (?<flags>[^ ]+) (?<log>.+)$
        Time_Key    time
        Time_Format %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%L
        Time_Keep   On

    [PARSER]
        Name    catchall
        Format  regex
        Regex   ^(?<message>.*)$
```

I would debug that by looking at your local config map to confirm things are correct first.
